payload.reason: The evidence indicates that the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) melts before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) due to specific geological and climatic conditions during the Last Interglacial (LIG) period, which are not merely for modeling convenience.

claims.text: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) begins to melt first, contributing to sea level rise at 126-124 ka, before the Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) starts melting at 118 ka.
The early melting of GrIS is linked to continental levering and ocean syphoning, which are significant geological processes affecting ice sheet dynamics.
